sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sin: sin (conj.) — but if, if on the other hand
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
sopitos: sōpiō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — to lull to sleep, deaden, quell (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
spes: spēs, speī (f.) — hope, expectation (nom. sg.; also acc. pl.)
stabat: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd sg. impf.)
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subducere: subdūcō, -ere, -duxī, -ductum — to draw up from below, haul ashore (pres. inf.)
sublime: sublīmis, -e — high, lofty, raised up (n. nom./acc. sg.; also adv. sublīme, aloft)
succincta: succingō, -ere, -cīnxī, -cīnctum — to gird up, equip (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; with abl.)
sustentat: sustentō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to hold up, sustain, support (3rd sg. pres.)
syrtis: Syrtis, -is (f.) — Syrtis, a quicksand, sandbank; the Syrtes (acc. pl., Greek -is = -ēs) · also nom. sg. (inhospita Syrtis)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talis: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) · also m./f. nom. sg. (talis erat Dido)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
telis: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (abl./dat. pl.)
tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)
tenuem: tenuis, -e — thin, slender, fine (m./f. acc. sg.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
teucrisque: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (dat./abl. pl.) + -que, and
timentem: timeō, -ēre, -uī — to fear, be afraid (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
tolle: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise, carry up (sg. imper.)
totumque: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n./m. acc. sg.) + -que 'and' · also n. nom. sg. (tōtum aequor)
trepida: trepidus, -a, -um — agitated, anxious, alarmed, in flurry (f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
tristia: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. pl.)
troianas: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. acc. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbidus: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, wild, confused, turbulent (m. nom. sg.)
turbo: turbō, -inis (m.) — whirlwind, storm, spinning blast (nom. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
ultra: ultrā (adv.) — beyond, further, more · also prep. + acc., beyond (vīrēs ultrā, beyond strength)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent)
utramque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (f. acc. sg.)
vana: vānus, -a, -um — empty, false, idle (f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
veri: vērus, -a, -um — true; vērum (n.), the truth (n. gen. sg., as noun)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertit: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — to turn, change (3rd sg. pres./perf.)
videbo: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. fut.)
video: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. pres.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres.: Vīs … vidēre?)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
vita: vīta, -ae (f.) — life, living; the breath of life (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
vivida: vīvidus, -a, -um — lively, vigorous, spirited (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vociferans: vōciferor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to cry aloud, shout (pres. part., f. nom. sg.) · also m. nom. sg.
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
volens: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, be willing (pres. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
volitare: volitō, -āre — to fly about, flit, flutter (pres. inf.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
